feature_coverage.delivered: Prompts are scanned for secrets (block by default), PII including TC Kimlik, IBAN and TR/international phones from the AIDR Privacy rules (warn by default) and tenant DLP, with kinds/counts only. Overlap resolution is a linear sort-and-sweep, a blocking scan stops at the first confirmed secret, and an internal deadline (default 7 s; the host kills the hook at 10 s) blocks an unfinished scan when secrets=block or a tenant DLP policy applies and otherwise sends the prompt with a visible not-fully-inspected notice; an incomplete personal-data scan is never reported clean. A DLP redact becomes an allow with rewritten input only where the host supports rewrite (Claude Code updatedInput, OpenCode args), using shell-inert REDACTED tokens, only if every parameter survives and the rewritten input rescans clean against DLP and the threat heuristics (dlp_redaction_unsafe otherwise); everything else is denied. Real-host records (linux/x64, development build, scripted mock model) show a prompt carrying a GitHub token never reaching the model on Claude Code 2.1.282, Codex CLI 0.141.0, OpenCode 1.18.32 and the OpenClaw 2026.9.6 embedded runner; pre-prompt is in the sold support matrix for those four connectors since 2026-09-30

feature_coverage.name: Session toxic-flow and behavioral chain detection

feature_coverage.remaining: Classification is heuristic and one level deep (bash -c, eval, argv, common prefixes); a custom binary that uploads data is not recognised as external communication, taint does not cross agent sessions or follow a moved/renamed download, and false-positive rates on real agent sessions are unmeasured

feature_coverage.name: Data and context poisoning protection
feature_coverage.consumer: Evaluator write/read paths, MCP gateway tool lists and package installs
feature_coverage.delivered: 23 CTX rules: write-time review of instruction, memory, agent-settings and MCP configuration files (a benign edit asks), read-time poisoned-context findings in tool output, hidden-Unicode detection, MCP tool-description poisoning and rug-pull checks through the gateway and signed manifests, memory/RAG write poisoning, and slopsquatting checks on young or unknown packages
feature_coverage.remaining: Pattern-based: a paraphrased instruction without a covered signal is caught only by the path-based review; shell writes built at run time are not attributed; tool descriptions are visible only through the MCP gateway or signed manifests; Codex has no read-time layer and enforces ask as deny; PyPI adoption uses release count because it has no download API

feature_coverage.name: Canary credentials (honeytokens)

feature_coverage.delivered: Six decoy kinds (AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, .env, SSH config, database URL) planted by an operator-only CLI with a digest-only registry; opening, searching or sending a decoy value is denied and recorded as a high-severity canary_triggered incident; an agent running aidr canary is blocked (CLT-CANARY-001); an unreadable registry is reported as canary_unavailable, never as clean
feature_coverage.remaining: A split, reversed or encrypted value is not recognised (base64 only from the start of the run); directory-wide reads that do not name a decoy are caught only in the tool output; relative paths match by trailing segments; Browser Guard treats decoys as ordinary secrets

feature_coverage.name: Agent-safety guardrails for autonomous agents
feature_coverage.consumer: Shared evaluator for every connector and the MCP gateway, local mode
feature_coverage.delivered: 43 rules and a session runaway guard: loops, repeated failures, rate spikes and optional budgets pause the session (ask); diff-aware reward-hacking checks (skipped tests, removed assertions, bypassed hooks, disabled CI, lowered coverage, blanket suppressions, force-push to protected branches) ask; launching an agent with approvals or sandbox off is denied; irreversible actions (drops, teardown, deletions, publishing, production deploys, payments) ask with an Irreversible action label
